passage:
A historic map showed a river flowing in the wrong direction. Students thought the mapmaker had been careless.
Their teacher explained that old maps were made from limited reports, travel stories, and measurements. Errors reveal what people did not yet know.
The class compared several maps from different years. The river slowly moved closer to its correct shape as explorers gathered better information.
The mistake became interesting instead of embarrassing.
Knowledge is often built through correction. A wrong map can show the path toward better understanding. Error, when preserved, becomes part of the history of learning.
